rankings.passage: During the period for which an F-1 student is granted post-completion optional practical training under this paragraph (f), an alien granted such employment authorization shall not accrue an aggregate of more than 90 days of unemployment during the initial post-completion optional practical training period approved by the United States Citizenship and Immigration Services.

The total period of post-completion practical training authorized under section 214.2(f)(10)(ii)(C) and the extension authorized under paragraph (f)(10)(ii)(C)(ii) of this section shall not exceed a cumulative maximum of 150 days of authorized unemployment during the entire period of post-completion optical training and the subsequent STEM extension combined.

The F-1 student may properly file an application for employment authorization pursuant to paragraph (f)(10)(ii)(A) of this section with the-designated service-center not earlier than 90 days prior to-the program end date-as determined by the-designated school official, nor later than 60 days following said program end date, provided that the application is received by the Service within 30 days of the date the endorsement for post-completion optional practical training was entered into the Student and Exchange Visitor Information System by the-designated school official.

The student who has failed to apply for employment authorization pursuant to paragraph (f)(10) of this section within the thirty-day period preceding the date of graduation and prior to the expiration of the sixty-day departure period following completion of the course of study is ineligible for post-completion practical training, and the SEVP portal shall reflect the termination of the student's maintaining of status.

The student must file the application for authorization for optional practical training with the Service within 30 days of the date the designated school official enters the recommendation for optional practical training into the student information system.

The student may request an optional practical training employment start date that is up to 60 days following the completion of the course of study, provided that the application is properly filed with the Service within the timeframe specified in paragraph (f)(11) of this section.

An eligible F-1 student enrolled in a science, technology, engineering, or math degree program may apply to the United States Citizenship and Immigration Services for a 24-month extension of post-completion practical training no earlier than 90 days prior to the expiration date of the student's current period of post-completion practical training.

An eligible F-1 student who files a timely application for a extension of temporary protected status or practical training under paragraph (f)(10)(ii)(C) of this section whose period of post-completion optional practical training has expired shall be authorized to continue employment for a period not to exceed 180 days beyond the expiration date of the previous optional practical training authorization, provided that the requirements of 8 CFR 274a.12(b)(6)(iv) are met, while the application remains pending with the Service.

The 24-month extension of post-completion optional practical training authorized under this paragraph (f) shall commence the day immediately following the expiration of the initial post-completion optional practical training employment authorization and shall conclude exactly twenty-four months thereafter, regardless of whether the student changes employers during such extended period of validity.

An F-1 student granted an extension of optical practical training under paragraph (f)(10)(ii)(C) of this section shall report to the student's designated school official a change of legal name, residential or mailing address, employer name, employer address, and/or loss of employment within 10 days of the change, and additionally shall validate the student's information every six months starting from the date the extension begins and ending when the extension terminates, in accordance with procedures established by the school.

Reporting requirements for extension. An approved student granted an extension of post-completion optional practical training under section 274(l) of the Act must provide a report to the designated school official of the student's current employment within 10 days of any change, including the loss of employment, termination of employment, or any change regarding the employer's name and address.

Reporting of physical address changes. An F-1 student granted extension of practical training under paragraph (f)(10)(i0) of this section shall report any change of legal name, residential or mailing address, employer name, and employer address to the designated school official within 10 days of the change, through the SEVIS reporting mechanism or such other form and manner as the Service may prescribe, until the conclusion of the authorized practical training period.

The F-1 student granted an extension of post-completion optional practical training under paragraph (f)(10)(ii)(C) of this section who changes employers during this extension period must submit, within 10 days of the change, a new Form I-983, Training Plan for STEM OPT Students, executed by the student and the new employer, to the designated school official of the school referred to in paragraph (f)(1)(i) of this section, reflecting the direct relationship between the student's degree and the new practical training opportunity.

The training plan for a student seeking an extension under paragraph (f)(10)(ii)(C) of this section must be formally completed by the employer and the student, signed by the designated school official, and submitted to the Service in accordance with instructions. The plan must clearly articulate the specific learning objectives directly related to the student's qualifying science, technology, engineering, or mathematics degree, delineate the detailed description of the mentorship and supervision provided by the employer, and establish performance evaluation criteria and standard oversight mechanisms to ensure the acquisition of targeted competencies throughout the duration of the practical training period.

The employer of a nonimmigrant student granted an extension of post-completion practical training pursuant to paragraph (f)(10)(ii)(C) of this section shall be enrolled in the E-Verify program administered by the Department of Homeland Security, as evidenced by a valid E-Verify company identification number or a valid E-Verify client company identification number, and shall remain in good standing with the E-Verify program as determined by the Department of Homeland Security throughout the duration of the extension.

For purposes of the post-completion extension of practical training described in paragraph (f)(10)(ii)(C) of this section, the student must be employed for a minimum of 20 hours per week by an employer that meets the qualifications set forth in paragraph (f)(10)(ii)(C)(3) of this section, and such employment must be directly related to the student's qualifying science, technology, engineering, or mathematics degree.

The student shall submit a self-evaluation assessing the progress of the training experience to the designated school official no later than 12 months after the start date of the approved extension and no later than 10 days following the conclusion of the training period or the termination of the Form I-20, whichever comes first, with each evaluation signed by both the student and the employer.

Reporting requirements for STEM optional practical training. An approved employer must notify the designated school official through the SEVP portal or other prescribed electronic reporting system within five business days of the termination or departure of an F-1 student granted an extension for practical training under paragraph (f)(10)(ii)(C) of this section, regardless of whether the termination is voluntary or involuntary on the part of the student.

For the purposes of the post-completion optional practical training extension under paragraph (f)(10)(ii)(C) of this section, qualifying degrees shall be limited to those designated by the Service as science, technology, engineering, or mathematics fields within the Department of Education's Classification of Instructional Programs normative taxonomy, denoting programs characterized by proficiency in domains encompassing research, innovation, or development using mathematical and natural sciences.

The cipher of an F-1 student currently maintaining status while completing a course of study leading to a master of business administration degree may not utilize a previously awarded baccalaureate degree in a science, technology, engineering, or mathematics field as the qualifying degree for a 24-month extension of post-completion optional practical training under paragraph (f)(10)(ii)(C) of this section, unless the qualifying degree forms the educational basis for the current course of study and was conferred by a certified school within the preceding ten years.

An eligible F-1 nonimmigrant student may be authorized a maximum of two post-completion periods of temporary training under section 101(a)(15)(F)(i)(II) of the Act based on a degree in a science, technology, engineering, or mathematics field, provided that the second such authorization follows a different qualifying degree at a higher educational level than the first.

An F-1 student who has completed a course of study and any authorized post-completion optional practical training under this paragraph is allowed a period of 60 days from the date of completion to depart the United States, apply for and obtain a change of status under 8 CFR 248, or transfer to another educational institution in accordance with paragraph (f)(8) of this section.

The period of post-completion optional practical training authorized under paragraph (f)(10)(ii)(A) of this section must be completed within a fourteen-month period following the student's program end date, except that an eligible student granted a 24-month extension under paragraph (f)(10)(ii)(C) of this section shall complete all authorized periods of practical training within the specified cumulative timeframe.

An eligible F-1 student may be authorized by the designated school official for part-time post-completion or pre-completion optional practical training, as described in paragraph (f)(10) of this section, while concurrently enrolled in a full course of study during the student's annual vacation or during the regular school term, provided that such employment does not exceed 20 hours per week while school is in session and is directly related to the student's major area of study.

Curricular practical training is defined to be employment which is an integral part of an established curriculum, including alternate work/study, internship, cooperative education, or any other type of required internship or practicum which is offered by sponsoring employers through cooperative agreements with the school. Such employment may be authorized by the designated school official to an eligible student who has been lawfully enrolled on a full-time basis, except during annual vacation, for one full academic year, provided that the training is directly related to the student's major area of study.

An eligible F-1 student who has been enrolled in a full-time course of study for one full academic year may be authorized for curricular practical training, provided, however, that an aggregate of one year or more of full-time curricular practical training authorized pursuant to this paragraph shall render the student ineligible for post-completion optional practical training described in paragraph (f)(10) of this section.

A student approved for attendance at an approved school may be employed on the campus of the school in which the student is registered, provided that such employment does not displace a United States resident and does not exceed 20 hours per week while school is in session, except during annual vacations and official school breaks, provided the student maintains a valid F-1 status and is in good academic standing.

The district director may, in his or her discretion, permit an F-1 student to engage in off-campus employment subsequent to acceptance of the Form I-20, Certification for Attendance, upon application containing evidence that the student has already suffered severe economic hardship caused by unexpected circumstances beyond the control of the student, including loss of assistantship or on-campus employment without fault on the part of the student, substantial fluctuations in the value of currency or exchange rate, unexpected changes in the financial condition of the student's source of support, medical bills, or other substantial and unexpected expenses.

Denial of an application for employment authorization pursuant to paragraph (f)(10) of this section shall not be subject to administrative appeal. The affected student may, however, request a motion to reopen or a motion to reconsider in accordance with the provisions of 8 CFR 103.5 governing such motions before the designated adjudicating authority within the period specified for such filings.

The transfer of a school or the beginning of a new program of study prior to the expiration date of authorized post-completion optional practical training shall automatically terminate the period of optional practical training.

An F-1 student on post-completion optional practical training may be readmitted to the United States for the remainder of the authorized period indicated on the Form I-20, provided the student presents a valid F-1 visa, a passport that is valid for at least six months from the date of admission, a Form I-20 endorsed for re-entry by the designated school official within the preceding six months, and a valid unexpired Employment Authorization Document issued by the Service.

An eligible F-1 student granted post-completion optional practical training may not engage in employment prior to the date indicated on the Employment Authorization Document issued by the Service, and no employment shall commence before the formal approval of the Form I-765 application and the physical receipt of the employment authorization card by the student.

Prior to recommending a student for a science, technology, engineering, or math optional practical training extension pursuant to paragraph (f)(10)(ii)(C) of this section, the designated school official shall ascertain that the student's degree is certified on the Science, Technology, Engineering, and Math Designated Degree Program List, that the employer is enrolled in the E-Verify program, that the compensation level is commensurate with similarly situated United States workers, and that the Form I-983 training plan has been properly completed and executed by the student and the prospective employer.

The Department of Commerce or the Department of Homeland Security may, at its discretion, conduct a site visit at any employer's place of business utilizing Form I-983 to ensure that the employer possesses and maintains the ability to provide structured and guided work-based learning experiences commensurate with the specified STEM extension period, provided that the employer is given a minimum of 48 hours notice, except in the case of a complaint or other evidence of noncompliance.

An eligible F-1 student may apply to the United States Citizenship and Immigration Services for authorization for pre-completion optional practical training up to 90 days prior to being enrolled for one full academic year, provided that the period of proposed practical training does not exceed the allowed limits and is recommended by the designated school official of the school in which the student is lawfully enrolled.
